title: bbox_thread mutations stall for the full duration of a slow edge-index rebuild
wanted_capability: Identification and removal of the shared resource that blocks bbox_thread mutations while an edge-index rebuild is in flight. Prod evidence (2026-08-23, cage daemon): three bbox_thread calls took 205s, 327s, and 169s, each completing within ~1 second of an edge-index rebuild finishing (271.6s, 374.9s, 194.6s rebuilds); tokio runtime metrics showed a core worker busy-blocked for the full 169s, so the handler blocks synchronously (a lock or lease, not an await). The rebuild's store read-guards drop before the multi-GB sidecar parse by design, so the contended resource is something held for the WHOLE rebuild (candidates: the index_writer publication guard's interaction with downstream paths, a Write-intent project-resolver lease, or the manifest coordinator). Phase-timing instrumentation (commit a3dbeb11) now logs which phase (resolve_project, store_write_guard, persist_durable) exceeds 5s; the next occurrence names the culprit.
fallback_used: Reduced rebuild frequency and duration by fixing the churn engines (marker retirement unwedging wampum, code-source probe); slow rebuilds were amplified by memory pressure near the 48Gi cgroup limit.
evidence: prod tool log: tool=bbox_thread elapsed_ms=327053 at 04:59:26.982, rebuild elapsed_ms=374852 finished 04:59:27.374
prod tool log: elapsed_ms=168998 at 05:11:13.123, rebuild elapsed_ms=194600 finished 05:11:14
notes: Triage trace: left open as uncertain. No fix has landed and no code on the bbox_thread or edge-rebuild paths (src/tools/threads.rs, src/server/routes.rs) changed since the previous triage. Static trace: the watcher rebuild (src/server/routes.rs spawn_edge_index_rebuild_watcher) runs on its own std thread and holds, for the whole rebuild, only the index_writer publication-activity reservation (try_begin_edge_index_rebuild, an atomic); store read guards (idx, kb, threads, notes, task_store) are held only during project_store_edges, and the manifest coordinator only at publish. In bbox_thread (src/tools/threads.rs), persist_threads_durable awaits a oneshot and index_writer.enqueue is a non-blocking send, so neither can busy-block a tokio worker; the busy-blocked worker therefore points at a synchronous phase: resolve_worktree_scope_and_dir (catalog snapshot, no lease), threads.write(), or thread_mutation itself (which writes the .bbox/record snapshot). Slow-phase instrumentation ('slow bbox_thread phase', over 5s) is in place. Production log checks (four consecutive triage runs; latest covers about 6.7h of retained logs on the current daemon pod): no 'slow bbox_thread phase' lines and no bbox_thread tool lines in the window; edge-index rebuilds peak near 20s; max tokio worker busy duration about 3.7s; the watcher defers most store-only nudges because the published sidecar graph exceeds its edge-count limit (routes.rs), which further reduces rebuild frequency. Still missing: one occurrence with a 'slow bbox_thread phase' line naming the blocked phase, or a bbox_thread call observed during a rebuild without a stall. Until one is observed the multi-minute stall cannot be confirmed or ruled out; with rebuilds bounded near 20s the premise may no longer hold.
